# Copilot Instructions — Pico-COMP

## Build
Run `./build.sh`: builds `comp_ui` and `comp_net` for the RP2350 RISC-V Hazard3 cores (`rp2350-riscv`, ARM is not used) into `build/`. Defaults: Pico SDK at `~/pico-sdk`, RISC-V toolchain at `~/toolchains/riscv` (override with `PICO_SDK_PATH`, `RISCV_TC`). Single target: `cmake --build build --target comp_ui` (or `comp_net`). The root project enables CXX/ASM only because the SDK requires it; project code is C. No tests or linter yet. KiCad and FreeCAD are installed for `hardware/`.

## Architecture
Two RP2350s (see `docs/architecture.md`): **UI** (`firmware/ui`: DVI/HSTX display, apps, printer/IO, SD) and **NET** (`firmware/net`: Wi-Fi via CYW43439, power, keyboard scan). They talk via the UART protocol in `firmware/common/link.h`. Hardware lives in `hardware/` (`kicad`, `mechanical` for FreeCAD, `keyboard`); plan in `docs/hardware-plan.md`. Display: 7" 1024x600 IPS HDMI LCD, 164.9 x 124.27 mm, 3.1 W at 5 V (capacitive touch unused) fed 720x400 DVI (fallback 640x480) by HSTX; its scaler fills the panel. Power: custom 2S2P 18650 pack with 5 V and 3.3 V bucks. The keyboard layout is generated by `hardware/keyboard/layout.py`; `gen_pcb.py` (needs KiCad's python, run `python3 hardware/keyboard/gen_pcb.py`) and `hardware/mechanical/case.py` (`FreeCADCmd hardware/mechanical/case.py`) both import it. Edit the layout and re-run; don't hand-edit `plate.dxf`, `matrix.csv` or `keyboard.kicad_pcb`.

## Project concept
Pico-COMP is a modern analog of the TRS-80 Model 100: a text-only, battery-powered portable built on a couple of Raspberry Pi RP2350 microcontrollers (user wrote "RP2530"; no such part exists, so RP2350 is assumed — confirm). Written exclusively in C (C11, Raspberry Pi Pico SDK with CMake); do not introduce C++, MicroPython, or other languages.

Hardware constraints from `intent.md` that should drive design decisions:
- ~10" simple monochrome LCD, text only; colour modes are amber-on-black, green-on-black, black-on-white.
- Small mechanical keyboard; arrow keys are the only navigation, with other functions on hotkeys (documented on a sticker by the screen base — keep hotkey assignments centrally defined so the sticker can be kept in sync).
- Power: 4× 18650 (1800 mAh), charged over USB-C; targets 1 week standby / 4 days of use, so favour low-power designs (sleep, minimal redraws, Wi-Fi only when needed).
- Wi-Fi: email, a few basic IM chats, and file sync by serving a web page on the local network.
- Can connect to printers and print documents.
- Beeps only for sound.

Planned software scope: text editor (also for writing code to continue on other machines), office suite (text documents, spreadsheets, database), email/IM, file sync web UI, basic text-based games, scheduler, todo app, printing.

Additional planned programs/features:
- Productivity: terminal/SSH client, calculator with a programmable BASIC-style interpreter, address book/phone list (syncable, label printing), notes with search plus outliner/journal, time tracker (integrated with scheduler/todo).
- Connectivity: RSS/news reader, Gopher/Gemini browser, IRC/Matrix client (for IM), serial/USB file transfer (e.g. XMODEM, USB mass-storage mode).
- Hardware: SD card storage, battery-backed RTC (alarms survive power-off), instant resume (save state to flash on sleep, restore on wake), battery gauge/status bar with low-battery auto-save, expansion port (GPS, sensors, barcode scanner) with a data logger app.
- Games/utilities: roguelike, text adventure, Tetris/Snake in character cells, typing tutor, Pomodoro timer, world clock.

## Conventions
- Keep everything text-mode and keyboard-only (no pointer/touch assumptions); every feature must be reachable via arrow keys + hotkeys.
- C only: all firmware, tooling glue, and libraries must be plain C.
- Memory and power are tight on microcontrollers: avoid heavy dependencies and dynamic allocation where practical.

## Display driver (firmware/ui)
- `dvi_text.{c,h}`: HSTX DVI text mode, 640x480@60, 80x30 cells, 8x16 font; scanlines rendered from a cell buffer in the DMA IRQ (no framebuffer). Schemes: amber/green/white via a 16-step intensity ramp.
- `font8x16.c` is generated by `tools/psf2c.py` from Terminus (OFL), CP437 order; do not hand-edit. Some CP437 box-drawing glyphs are blank.
- Untested on hardware. 720x400 (80x25, 9px font) is still planned and needs PLL/sys-clock changes.

## Case viewer
`FreeCADCmd hardware/mechanical/case.py` writes the STEP, FCStd and `assembly.json`; `python3 hardware/mechanical/build_viewer.py` builds the offline `pico-comp-viewer.html`. The lid carries a Wi-Fi antenna pocket in the right bezel (beside, never behind, the panel).
